answer: Honeypot audits turn cloned graders into a liability. The network mixes juniper items, answers with a known true score, into every grading queue at a one-in-ten rate. Each copy carries a pigment, a per-grader watermark in the item text, so a rationale that echoes another grader's pigment proves copying. When k graders return the same wrong score on one juniper item, the willow rule slashes each of them k stakes. Ten coordinated clones lose 100 stakes per caught item; an honest grader who errs alone loses one.
